title: Directly detect the cosmic neutrino background

concept.text: The innovation is to directly detect relic neutrinos left over from the early universe by measuring a distinctive physical signal and establishing its relic-neutrino origin. The intended advance is an observation of the background itself, beyond indirect cosmological evidence consistent with its existence. The supplied research identifies neutrino capture as one possible detection route while allowing another sufficiently distinctive physical signature.

The central measurement challenge is to distinguish an exceptionally weak signal from radioactive decay backgrounds and instrumental effects. A convincing result would connect the observed signature, its calibration and its measured properties to a relic-neutrino interpretation. This is the scientific concept described in the supplied materials; those materials contain no retained source passages independently substantiating its technical premises.

significance.text: Conditional on establishing a relic-neutrino origin, direct detection would open an additional observational channel associated with conditions in the universe’s first seconds. The supplied research contrasts this with the much later cosmic microwave background: the significance would come from gaining access to a different physical messenger of early cosmic history. The review considers this reasoning coherent, while noting that the supplied source record does not independently substantiate the timing or the technical comparison.

As a capability assessment, the revolutionary step would be to turn a cosmologically inferred population into something directly measurable. Further scientific returns would depend on which properties the instrument could resolve and how securely those properties could be interpreted. Detection would not automatically provide a spatial image of the early universe, establish every neutrino property or settle unrelated cosmological questions.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a sufficiently sensitive measurement that can both reveal a candidate relic-neutrino signal and distinguish it from competing explanations. The supplied research identifies extremely low neutrino energies and exceptionally weak interactions as the underlying obstacles. These premises explain the difficulty of the proposed experiment, but no retained technical source in this record supplies numerical energies, expected event rates or detector requirements.

For the proposed capture route, the concrete barriers include separating the capture signature from radioactive decay backgrounds, controlling instrumental effects and independently calibrating the measurement at the sensitivity required. Improving background rejection or demonstrating a detector component would be enabling progress; completion also requires evidence that the surviving signal has the expected physical origin. The supplied materials do not establish which target strategy, detector configuration or attainable precision can meet that requirement.

current_state.text: The supplied research describes cosmological observations as providing indirect evidence consistent with a relic neutrino background and identifies PTOLEMY as pursuing direct detection. It also attributes target-strategy work to the project’s 2026 website updates and states that the project was not reporting a relic-neutrino detection. However, the source index contains no retained website content, and the review could not verify those statements or their freshness. They should therefore be read as reported research context, rather than a confirmed account of the project’s present capabilities.

The research identifies the paper “Upper limits on the cosmic neutrino background from cosmic rays,” dated 23 September 2024, as a complementary constraint. It describes the paper as deriving upper limits under model assumptions, rather than reporting a direct detection. That distinction matters: a bound on an allowed background is a different scientific result from observing relic neutrinos. No paper text was retained in the supplied record, so its specific findings, assumptions, numerical bounds and publication date were not independently verified in the review.

The earlier research also reports a 502 access error for an INFN project description and says detailed demonstrator readiness could not be independently checked. The supplied review could not substantiate the access event itself, because no supporting artifact was retained. More broadly, the empty search record prevents a freshness assessment as of 1 November 2026. The materials therefore establish neither a verified direct detection nor a verified up-to-date account of experimental readiness; this evidence limitation does not show that the reported project work or scientific results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: observe a reproducible signal with the expected relic-neutrino capture signature, or another comparably distinctive physical signature, and establish an independently calibrated separation from radioactive and instrumental backgrounds. The evidence should show why known backgrounds and plausible alternative explanations cannot adequately account for the observation. These are proposed criteria for a convincing result, not an established published standard.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible distinctive relic-neutrino signal independently separated from known backgrounds

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation should test the signal’s rate and measurable properties against the relic-neutrino interpretation and relevant alternatives, with uncertainties and instrumental limitations stated explicitly. Reproducibility should allow independent validation through another instrument, a different implementation or sufficiently independent calibration and analysis; it need not require identical equipment.
completion_criteria.label: Signal rate and properties tested with independently reproducible validation

completion_criteria.text: A completion claim should specify what was actually demonstrated: the operating conditions, sensitivity, tested backgrounds and physical properties constrained. The supplied materials justify no numerical threshold for significance, exposure or precision, so none is prescribed here. Finite tests would establish the breadth of the demonstrated result, while leaving untested conditions and unresolved interpretive assumptions visible.
completion_criteria.label: Demonstrated detection scope reported with limits and unresolved assumptions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AST-09, “Make neutrino astronomy capable of routinely resolving hidden cosmic sources,” shares neutrino detection, calibration and background-control challenges. Its objective is routine observation of cosmic sources; AST-12 concerns identifying a relic background associated with the early universe. Progress in detector technology may be relevant to both, but achieving either objective would not by itself complete the other.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-05, “Detect and identify a primordial gravitational-wave background,” is closely related as a search for a background that could reveal early cosmic conditions. The two concepts involve different messengers and different evidence for origin. AST-10, “Open the millihertz gravitational-wave sky as a working observatory,” likewise concerns opening an observational channel, but its completion requires an operating observatory capability rather than identification of the relic-neutrino background.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-03, “Identify the physical constituent of astronomical dark matter,” and AST-04, “Establish the physical cause of cosmic acceleration,” overlap with AST-12 through fundamental cosmology. Direct relic-neutrino detection could add cosmological information, but it would not automatically identify dark matter or explain cosmic acceleration. AST-06, “Map the cosmic dark ages and first luminous structures in three dimensions,” concerns spatial reconstruction of later cosmic history; the proposed relic-neutrino measurement does not itself supply such a map. These remain distinct entries and scientific objectives.

brief.title: Direct detection of particles from the early universe
possible: People could directly measure neutrinos left over from the early universe: elusive particles that interact exceptionally weakly. A distinctive signal would turn a population inferred from cosmology into something instruments can detect.
why: Scientists would gain a physical messenger from the universe’s first seconds. It would offer access to an earlier period than the cosmic microwave background, the light left over from a later stage of cosmic history.

sources.showed: A project pursuing direct detection of neutrinos left over from the early universe.
sources.cited_for: PTOLEMY is pursuing the experimental route to direct detection.
sources.not_established: Pursuing an experiment does not establish a signal from relic neutrinos.

sources.who: Authors of “Upper limits on the cosmic neutrino background from cosmic rays”
sources.showed: A study derives upper limits on the relic-neutrino background under model assumptions.
sources.cited_for: Model-dependent limits provide a complementary constraint on the background.
sources.not_established: An upper limit constrains how much background could exist; it does not directly detect it.

shown: Cosmological observations provide indirect evidence consistent with a background of leftover neutrinos. PTOLEMY is pursuing direct detection, while a separate study derives model-dependent upper limits. Neither amounts to an established direct detection.
missing: A measurement sensitive enough to reveal these exceptionally weakly interacting, low-energy particles.
A distinctive signal separated from radioactive decay and instrumental effects through independent calibration.
Tests showing that the signal’s rate and properties fit leftover neutrinos better than plausible alternatives.

milestones.label: A repeatable signal distinguishable from known backgrounds
milestones.explanation: A repeatable signal from neutrino capture, or another distinctive physical process, would need independently calibrated separation from known backgrounds. This would establish a credible candidate detection.

milestones.label: Independent validation of the signal’s rate and properties
milestones.explanation: Independent tests would have to reproduce the signal’s rate and measurable properties and compare them with competing explanations. This would test whether leftover neutrinos explain the observation.

milestones.label: A detection with clearly demonstrated scope and limits
milestones.explanation: A detection claim would have to state its operating conditions, sensitivity, tested backgrounds and constrained physical properties. This would define what the result establishes and which assumptions remain unresolved.

uncertain: Which target and detector design can achieve the sensitivity and background separation needed for detection remains unresolved.
No numerical threshold for declaring detection is established, including the required precision or strength of evidence.
The further scientific return depends on which neutrino properties an instrument can resolve and how securely they can be interpreted.

page.title: Direct detection of the cosmic neutrino background
page.definition: Neutrinos left from the early Universe are observed through their interactions with a detector. The cosmic neutrino background is the population that ceased exchanging energy efficiently with the primordial plasma about one second after the Big Bang.

goal.need: Relic neutrinos carry information from an earlier epoch than cosmic microwave background photons. Direct detection tests whether this population survives today and measures its local abundance. Standard cosmology predicts about 336 neutrinos and antineutrinos per cm³, but an ideal 100 g tritium target captures only about 4 or 8 per year for unclustered, non-relativistic Dirac or Majorana neutrinos, respectively.

completion.title: Primordial relic neutrinos are directly detected at a significance of at least 5σ.
completion.criterion: Directly observe an interaction signal attributable to primordial relic neutrinos, rejecting the background-only hypothesis with one-sided significance Z ≥ 5, corresponding to p ≤ 2.87 × 10⁻⁷. Include background-model uncertainties and applicable search-trial corrections. For tritium capture, establish a nonzero relic-neutrino capture component above the beta-decay endpoint, distinguishable from beta-spectrum leakage and other backgrounds.
completion.set_by: Particle-physics discovery convention documented by the Particle Data Group, Statistics (2025), §40.3.2; the capture-component test is specified by PTOLEMY's 2019 analysis, §§4 and 6.
completion.threshold_quote: is Z = 5, i.e., a 5σ effect, corresponding to a p-value of 2.87 × 10−7.
completion.basis: This applies the particle-physics discovery convention to PTOLEMY's test of a nonzero capture contribution; it is not a CNB-specific certification rule. Significance is conditional on the background model and does not alone identify relic origin. The cosmic-ray study published on 23 September 2024 derives overdensity limits, rather than reporting relic-neutrino capture.

milestones.title: Individual electrons are detected through their cyclotron radiation.
milestones.criterion: Detect radio-frequency radiation from individual magnetically trapped electrons and reconstruct their kinetic energies from the cyclotron frequency. Project 8 reported this on 20 April 2015 using krypton-83m conversion electrons; its 30.4 keV lines reached 15 eV full width at half maximum. PTOLEMY's proposal recognises this component demonstration and requires subsequent integration.
milestones.set_by: PTOLEMY collaboration, published 2018 experimental proposal, Introduction and §7; identifies Project 8's single-electron demonstration as an enabling result.
milestones.threshold_quote: single electron RF detection has been successfully achieved

milestones.title: A PTOLEMY endpoint-measurement demonstrator reaches 0.05 eV energy resolution or better.
milestones.criterion: Integrate a graphene source, magnetic/electrostatic filter and transition-edge-sensor calorimeter in an endpoint-measurement system with energy resolution of 0.05 eV or better. A transition-edge sensor measures deposited heat near a superconducting transition. The integration paragraph does not specify standard deviation versus full width at half maximum. On 29 October 2024, Pepe et al. reported one 100 × 100 µm² Ti/Au sensor with Gaussian energy resolution of 0.8–1.8 eV for fully absorbed 90–101 eV electrons.
milestones.set_by: PTOLEMY collaboration, published 2018 experimental proposal, §9, integrated endpoint-measurement goal.
milestones.threshold_quote: an energy resolution of 0.05 eV or better.

milestones.title: A relic-neutrino capture detector operates with at least 100 g of tritium.
milestones.criterion: Operate the capture detector with at least 100 g of tritium and approximately energy-independent non-beta background no greater than about 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹ over the 15 eV endpoint region used in PTOLEMY's 2019 study. Its illustrative exposure is one year. These are that design's requirements, not universal lower bounds or sufficient discovery conditions. The collaboration's 2026 report describes its demonstrator as under construction. A 2022 analysis requires full width at half maximum ≲20 meV under its standard-cosmology assumptions.
milestones.set_by: PTOLEMY collaboration, 2019 physics study, §4; requirements for its tritium-capture design.
milestones.threshold_quote: a tritium mass of at least 100 g

milestones.title: A direct relic-neutrino signal reaches at least 3σ significance.
milestones.criterion: Observe a positive relic-neutrino interaction contribution at significance Z ≥ 3, using the particle-physics evidence convention. For tritium capture, test a nonzero capture contribution against beta decay and other backgrounds, including nuisance parameters and applicable search-trial corrections. This is an observed-signal milestone; a projected sensitivity or an upper limit does not satisfy it.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics evidence convention documented by CERN in its Bulletin of 16 April 2001; applied to PTOLEMY's published capture-component test.
milestones.threshold_quote: Three sigma or more is considered evidence for a new phenomenon
